newsitem.title: USA: US FERC sets two capacity release pilot programs.
newsitem.headline: US FERC sets two capacity release pilot programs.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved two interstate natural gas pilot programs to test pipeline companies' plans to lift price caps on rates charged for released pipeline capacity.

The commission approved a joint application by Transwestern Pipeline Co, a subsidiary of Enron Corp, Pacific Gas and Electric Co and Southern California Gas Co to operate a pilot program to serve western markets.
FERC also approved a joint application filed by Columbia Gas Transmission System and Mountaineer Gas Co, a subsidiary of Allegheny & Western Energy Corp, for a test program mainly in eastern markets.
The commission previously has blocked gas shippers from charging more than a pipeline's regulated rates when they rent to other shippers space which they have reserved on interstate pipelines.

In July, the commission asked for applicants to operate pipeline programs that would lift the price cap for released capacity and interruptible and short-term firm transportation in markets where the applicant can show it lacked market power.
The pilot programs are intended to test criteria for evaluating market power, based on actual experience, before the commission enacts a final rule.

Under standards the commission set in July, applicants had to provide data showing pipelines and local distribution companies lacked market power, and information showing that the LDC provided an acceptable open-access transportation service.

Participating pipelines also were to agree to implement tariff provisions streamlining capacity release procedures, and to provide detailed transaction data for the term of the pilot program and one year before the program's start.

The commission rejected applications filed by Kern River Transmission Co, Arizona Public Service Co, Boston Gas Co, a subsidiary of Eastern Enterprises, and a joint proposal by Transcontinental Gas Pipeline Co, a subsidiary of Williams Cos Inc, Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Washington Gas Light and National Fuel Gas Distribution Corp.
